newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY LEAGUE-WEST OUSTED AT WIGAN AFTER 14 YEARS.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY LEAGUE-WEST OUSTED AT WIGAN AFTER 14 YEARS.

text.p: New Zealander Graeme West was deposed as coach of Wigan on Monday after 14 years with English rugby league's most successful club.
West was offered a desk job in the wake of Wigan's cup defeat to St Helens earlier this month but declined to take it and has been replaced by his assistant Eric Hughes.
"I've had some great times at Wigan and I'm thankful for that," said West, who joined the club as a player in 1982 and took over as coach from Australian John Dorahy in 1994.
"But it's a volatile job and this would probably have come sooner or later. It's just one of those things."

West argues his hands have been tied by Wigan's recent financial problems and the temporary loss of star players like Gary Connolly, Henry Paul, Va'aiga Tuigamala and Jason Robinson to rugby union this season.
The Super League dispute in Australia cost the club huge sums in loyalty payments and West says Wigan's problems are mirrored elsewhere.
"A lot of clubs have got to get their books in order and then go out looking for players they can afford," he said.
